articles.title: Anthropic says it’s committing 5% of its shares to a ‘public benefit fund’
articles.full_text:
Anthropic announced today that it’s creating a “public benefit fund” that will give the company “increased flexibility and scale” to support projects for societal good.

Anthropic said that it will commit 5% of its shares to the fund — structured as a wholly-owned entity within the company — with the option to contribute an additional 2% for every 50% increase in Anthropic’s value. And it offered some broad-strokes ideas for how this money might actually be used, such as “large donations to traditional nonprofits or direct distributions to specific populations.”

There’s also the impact that AI might have on the job market, which Anthropic has already committed $200 million to study. But the company said, “Given the pace of AI progress, bolder approaches may be needed. The Fund will have the versatility to pursue them.”

Anthropic’s announcement comes as the AI industry faces increasingly negative public sentiment, which CEO Dario Amodei has described as “fundamentally a crisis of trust.”

If you’re wondering who will actually decide which public benefits are worth funding, Anthropic said it will share more information about structure and governance in the coming months.
articles.summary:
Anthropic has announced the creation of a "public benefit fund" designed to give the company greater flexibility and scale to support projects for societal good. The move comes as the AI industry confronts growing public skepticism, which CEO Dario Amodei has called "fundamentally a crisis of trust."

  • Core commitment: Anthropic will contribute 5% of its shares to the fund, structured as a wholly-owned entity within the company, with the option to add another 2% for every 50% increase in Anthropic's value.
  • Intended uses: The company offered broad-strokes ideas for deploying the money, such as large donations to traditional nonprofits or direct distributions to specific populations, while noting the fund's versatility could support bolder approaches given the pace of AI progress.
  • Background: Anthropic has already committed $200 million to study AI's potential impact on the job market, and the new fund is positioned as a way to pursue more ambitious efforts as public sentiment toward AI grows increasingly negative.
  • Open questions: Anthropic said it will share more information about the fund's structure and governance in the coming months, leaving unclear who will ultimately decide which public benefits are worth funding.
